instructions.question: Does this passage cite or refer to another document or provision?
instructions.passage: Subsequent reference to a statutory section is to the Public Utilities Code, unless otherwise specified.

instructions.question: Does this passage cite or refer to another document or provision?
instructions.passage:
Section 739.5(a) states as follows:
“The commission shall require that whenever gas or electric service, or both, is provided by a master-meter customer to users who are tenants of a mobilehome park, apartment building, or similar residential complex, the master-meter customer shall charge each user of the service at the same rate which would be applicable if the user were receiving gas or electricity, or both, directly from the gas or electrical corporation.  The commission shall require the corporation furnishing service to the master-meter customer to establish uniform rates for master-meter service at a level which will provide a sufficient differential to cover the reasonable average costs to master-meter customers of providing submeter service, except that these costs shall not exceed the average cost that the corporation would have incurred in providing comparable services directly to the users of the service.” (Pub. Util. Code § 739.5 subd. (a).)

instructions.question: Does this passage cite or refer to another document or provision?
instructions.passage: FOF No. 33 states as follows:  “Section 739.5 applies to a limited set of residential users; tenants of master-metered MHPs, in this case, and does not apply to the general body of ratepayers.” (D.04-11-033, p. 35.)

instructions.question: Does this passage cite or refer to another document or provision?
instructions.passage: Subsection (b) of Section 739.5 deals with the distribution of utility rebates between master-meter customers and their tenants or users; subsection (c) concerns provision of public safety information to such users; subsection (d) imposes maintenance responsibilities for the sub-metered facilities on the master-meter customer; and subsection (e) requires itemized billing from the master-meter customer to its users.

instructions.question: Does this passage cite or refer to another document or provision?
instructions.passage: COL No. 11 states as follows:  “The term “comparable services” refers to services provided to directly-served MHP customers of the utility, as opposed to residential ratepayers as a whole.”

instructions.question: Does this passage cite or refer to another document or provision?
instructions.passage: The extent of the distortion is illustrated in PG&E’s Response to WMA’s application.  It notes that submetering discount for apartment buildings is $0.10579 per space per day, but that the MHP submetering discount is $0.34300 per space per day; and that under WMA’s position the discounts would be set at the same level.

instructions.question: Does this passage cite or refer to another document or provision?
instructions.passage: The Joint Motion stated that this issue is very complex and could require additional weeks of hearings.  (Motion of Joint Parties to Establish Separate Proceeding, filed Jan. 16 2004,    p. 4.)

instructions.question: Does this passage cite or refer to another document or provision?
instructions.passage:
The three findings state the following:
There is no significant potential for increased utility revenues because of such a transfer because the utility already provides the same amount of electricity or natural gas to the MHP owner at the master-meter as would subsequently be provided directly as a result of the transfer.

instructions.question: Does this passage cite or refer to another document or provision?
instructions.passage: The fact that the utility would no longer have to pay the discount is offset by the costs, related to providing service directly, that were previously provided by the MHP owner.

instructions.question: Does this passage cite or refer to another document or provision?
instructions.passage: Since there is no apparent benefit to the stockholders resulting from the transfer, there is no apparent reason why they should bear any of the costs.
